operators.name: embedding_forward

parameters.name: indices
parameters.shape: same as reference input x, e.g. [batch_size, input_length]
parameters.layout: contiguous (reference input is contiguous, but supports arbitrary strides via explicit handling or contiguous call)

returns.shape: same as reference embedding output: indices.shape + [embedding_dim]

semantics: Equivalent to torch.nn.functional.embedding(indices, weight) with padding_idx not specified
For each element in indices, output[..., :] = weight[indices[element], :]
Indices are int64; output is float32 on CUDA
No gradient or training mode semantics in forward
Embedding lookup: output[i, j, :] = embedding.weight[x[i, j], :]
Input x shape [1024,512] int64; output shape [1024,512,300] float32
Device becomes CUDA because model/weight moved to CUDA and input is moved to CUDA by framework
No dimension of size 1, so shape remains [1024,512,300]
Returns tensor of shape [1024,512,300], dtype float32, device cuda:0
